channel.title: SigilForge Studios News
channel.description: Development logs, release notices, recovered transmissions, and changes to the Archive.

item.title: Book One becomes CradlePoint: VeilSight
item.description: Book One is now CradlePoint: VeilSight, rebuilt as a v48 second edition with a new cover, new title matter, and a device readout that finally says VEILSIGHT: ACTIVE. The prose is unchanged. Buyers get the full bundle, including PDF, EPUB, MOBI, and a re-lettered wallpaper pack, and its Creator Rights Record keeps its permanent URL, adding version 2 instead of rewriting version 1.

item.title: Brand state locked in
item.description: Every surface now wears the mark that owns it. SigilForge Studios on the Studio pages, the registry, Creator Rights, and VeilLink. VeilCorp on the VeilDaemon terminal. CradlePoint only where a page is explicitly about CradlePoint. The last "Cradlepoint Studio" remnants were removed, the press kit was rebuilt from the real masters, and the Witness Key's WE WITNESS ring was corrected.

item.title: Storefront and VeilLink reorganized
item.description: VeilLink became an umbrella portal, with /home as the signed-in hub instead of a page pretending to be a single product. The SigilForge storefront got clear paths for Book One, the TTRPG, Operator and Handler, VeilLink, and VeilDaemon. Web design became a real offer, with fixed packages, direct checkout, and a text-message contact route for people who do not want another form.

item.title: Daily commentary finds its shape
item.description: After the first Dispatch, a daily rhythm settled in. Each piece gives one character, speaking through one Frequency, a reaction to something happening in the real world: KIRA // VOID, KAELYN // BECOMING, ALEX // SILENCE, WEDNESDAY // BECOMING.

item.title: Archive Notes become a publishing cadence
item.description: Father Samiel on the 12th, Alex on the 13th, Diana on the 14th, the first weekly Dispatch on the 15th, and Wednesday on the 16th. Each note started as something small enough to pass through a social feed and then followed it into the Archive. This is the point where characters speaking through the Archive became a recognizable public format instead of a one-off. Every note opens free.

item.title: Cell / Live-Link networking goes live
item.description: The Operator and Handler apps started talking to each other across devices. Handler mechanical authority now reaches the Operator live, a real remote transport replaced the old export-and-import ferry, rolls report across devices, a lobby-wide roll feed runs in real time, and the Handler holds authority over the round. A table no longer has to share a screen to share a session.

item.title: SigilForge Rights Framework 1.0
item.description: The SigilForge Rights Framework and the guided Creator Rights Record workflow became publicly usable, which put Creator Rights in its public-launch state. The same day the licensing split around VeilDaemon and VeilForge was corrected. VeilForge's record now reads proprietary, not MPL-2.0.

item.title: Creator Rights Registry publicly live
item.description: The registry opened with 12 records. It has searchable filtering, permanent /rights/<slug>/ pages, JSON metadata, QR destinations, declared AI-use permissions, and version history.

item.title: Creator Rights Records, phase one
item.description: The registry, the public Studio page, JSON records, VeilLink APIs, the database schema with row-level security, and QR export all merged. It was built that day, not launched. The public opening came two days later.

item.title: SigilForge Studios
item.description: The studio stopped calling itself Cradlepoint Studio. SigilForge Studios became the umbrella over CradlePoint, VeilDaemon, VeilLink, and VeilForge, while VeilCorp stayed where it belongs, on the terminal. The emblem took 147 attempts.

item.title: Archive Lattice Revision
item.description: Shade transmission: sealed recovery vault, VeilLink identity binding, ownership imprint, and expandable publishing lattice. STATUS: STABLE. For now.

item.title: Book One Digital Release Infrastructure Complete
item.description: First full version of SigilForge Studios digital publishing infrastructure for Book One and future Archive recoveries. One live acquisition cycle remains.

item.title: Why VeilLink Exists
item.description: VeilLink is the identity tether that lets the Archive remember ownership across books, Needlepoints, audio, and future recoveries.

item.title: From One Book to VeilBorn Publishing
item.description: How an ISBN pricing complaint escalated into private vaults, ownership imprints, and VeilBorn Publishing.

item.title: Current SigilForge Studios Roadmap
item.description: Books, TTRPG, VeilDaemon, VeilLink, print, audio, and the Archive client — one connected universe.

item.title: Book One enters production
item.description: The complete Book One manuscript and its character artwork were consolidated into the production repository, and the editing sources were collapsed into a single v26 line. The v0.4 build was documented on the 17th, and the paid launch packs were refreshed on the 18th.

item.title: The Studio gets a front door
item.description: The Studio pages went up: projects, publishing, funding, a public data room, privacy and terms. A day later came the press room, the technology page, the founder story, and VeilForge. This is where the site started behaving like the front door of a studio rather than a strange terminal someone found in a ditch. It launched under the Cradlepoint Studio name, which lasted thirteen days.

item.title: Commercial release
item.description: The Handler Core release pack was built and launched. The storefront went live with Operator Core ($15) and Handler Core ($20) beside the free Needlepoint on-ramp. Counts at launch: 25 final PDFs, 132 wiki articles, 47 VeilDaemon surfaces, 85 automated tests, 8 core manuscripts, 2 free Needlepoints, 2 paid release lanes.

item.title: The live Handler runtime takes shape
item.description: Over six days the Handler side gained an attention system, Needlepoint templates, NPC and entity handling, Operator trackers, Collapse and Rewrite staging, anchors, and Clue Integrity. Then came the Presentation Pressure framework and a universal Load architecture across the presentations, with Sanguine the first to load against it. By July 1, the runtime at the table was substantially the one in use now.

item.title: VeilDaemon becomes an Operator system
item.description: Intake gating came first, followed by Operator files that can be exported, imported, and equipped. Active Misfire and Lotus expression arrived, along with provenance, debrief intake with redaction review, and the recovered-reports index. The Handler Dashboard landed on June 24. Saves stay local by default.

item.title: Release-candidate stabilization
item.description: The public digest set the bar for everything shipped so far: downloadable, printable, runnable. What followed was cleanup, with no new surface area.

item.title: Viridian House is table-ready
item.description: The free CradlePoint pack was updated with handouts and Handler tools for Viridian House. VeilDaemon is named in it as the public intake and routing interface, alongside the wiki and the free download.

item.title: The intake terminal
item.description: The VeilDaemon site went up with an interactive intake console in place of a form. Observer routing starts here.

item.title: VeilCorp Training_404
item.description: VeilCorp Training_404 went out. By this point the public framing was explicit: a myth-tech horror TTRPG.

item.title: Entity File: Sanguine
item.description: Sanguine was transmitted as a public Archive release. The free first-contact materials were already being pointed to from the Archive.

item.title: The CradlePoint wiki
item.description: The CradlePoint Archives wiki was approved and created.

item.title: Needlepoint becomes playable by outside tables
item.description: Polished case files went live on itch.io: Player Quickshot, GM Quickshot, the case file, handouts, the GM toolbox, and release notes. This was the line between something the author could run and something any table could pick up and playtest. Office Transmission_003 went public around the same time.

item.title: Office Broadcast 002
item.description: The Partial Recovery and Full Recovery transmissions were published, and NEEDLEPOINT was presented as the first public quickstart.

item.title: The CradlePoint Archives opens
item.description: The Archive opened publicly on Patreon, with Needlepoint and Devlog 01 already part of the presentation. This is the earliest point with a continuous public record, so this record starts here.

item.title: Before the Archive Opened
item.description: Two years before the public record: project inception, Resonance of the Void becoming Book One, the VeilDaemon repository, VeilForge, and the TTRPG corpus.
